parsed.headline: President Mahama travels to Egypt for Eighth AU Mid-Year Coordination Summit

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama is in Alamein, Egypt, to participate in the Eighth African Union (AU) Mid-Year Coordination Summit. According to a statement issued by the Presidency, the summit opens on Saturday. The Heads of State gathering for the summit is scheduled for September 27, 2026. During the summit, President Mahama is expected to hold bilateral meetings on the sidelines, including a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. The gatherings aim to advance African economic integration and sustainable development while providing a platform for governments, businesses, and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities and strengthen partnerships.

In addition to the AU summit, President Mahama will join the maiden Alamein Africa Forum, which is running parallel to the AU Heads of State Summit. The Presidency stated that the Alamein Africa Forum opens with an address by the President of Egypt and a keynote by Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote. President Mahama is scheduled to deliver a keynote at a plenary session titled “Investing in Health: Manufacturing and Regional Value Chains,” where he will examine health as an investable market and strategic economic sector rather than just a social expenditure.

parsed.headline: Two Iranian men charged in alleged Manchester synagogue bomb plot

pages.text: Two Iranian men appeared in Westminster Magistrates' Court on a Saturday morning, facing charges of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism. Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, of Liverpool, were charged on October 2, 2026, in connection with an alleged plot targeting the Jewish community in Manchester. Prosecutors allege the men were preparing attacks involving a homemade explosive device, which could have been manufactured using chlorine and brake fluid. The court heard the pair allegedly conducted hostile reconnaissance of potential targets, including the Heaton Park synagogue and the Manchester Jewish Museum. The charges relate to alleged conduct carried out on or before September 20, the eve of Yom Kippur. Prosecutors further allege the men were in contact with a third party believed to be operating from within Iran, who directed and coordinated the planned attack and provided instructions on preparing an explosive device. Both defendants were remanded in custody and did not enter pleas during the hearing. Salehi arrived in the UK in 2020 and was granted leave to remain in 2023, while Ahmadyan arrived in 2023 and has an outstanding asylum claim. The court heard both men entered the UK via small boats.

parsed.headline: Indian High Commissioner states there was no alternative but to allow Sheikh Hasina to land in Delhi

pages.text: Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi stated there was no alternative but to allow former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina to land in Delhi, asserting that refusing her landing would have created a different situation. Speaking during a question-and-answer session at the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026 at a Dhaka hotel on Saturday afternoon, Trivedi said that when Hasina left Dhaka, she was still the prime minister of Bangladesh and India was not prepared for the situation. He noted that she arrived in India on a Bangladeshi military aircraft and that, as a neighboring country, India had few options other than accepting the reality of the arrival. Trivedi added that he did not know what the situation would have been if India had refused to allow the landing. Regarding the potential extradition of the ousted prime minister, Trivedi said the Indian government has stated through its Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson that a legal process is currently underway based on a specific framework. He noted that because the courts are involved, no specific timeline can be provided for the matter.

parsed.headline: Experts call for long-term policy certainty to meet Bangladesh renewable energy targets

pages.text: During a webinar organized by the Dacca Institute of Research and Analytics (daira) on October 2, 2026, speakers highlighted the need for long-term policy certainty, grid modernization, energy storage, and private-sector investment to accelerate Bangladesh’s transition toward renewable energy. The session, titled “Bangladesh's Renewable Energy Transition: Closing the Gap to 2030, and the Economic Opportunity Ahead,” addressed the gap between current capacity and national ambitions, as well as the implications of continued dependence on imported fossil fuels. According to a policy brief presented by daira researcher Suborna Akther Laboni, renewable energy currently accounts for approximately 2.3 per cent of Bangladesh’s grid electricity, while the government has set a target of 20 per cent by 2030. To remain on track for this target, approximately 760 MW of renewable energy would need to be added annually, compared to the 358 MW under construction as of February 2026. Meeting the 2030 goal is estimated to require an annual investment of US$933–980 million through 2030.

parsed.headline: Israeli military reports killing two Islamic Jihad commanders in Gaza City airstrikes

pages.text: The Israeli military stated on Saturday that it killed two commanders within the Islamic Jihad movement's rocket system during two airstrikes targeting Gaza City on October 2, 2026. According to a military statement, the first strike killed Ahmed Mahmoud Harb al-Ramlawi, identified as a commander in the rocket unit of the Shuja’iyya Battalion, which is part of the movement’s military wing. A second strike in Gaza City killed Munir Ibrahim al-Masri, who the military reported headed an anti-tank missile cell within the movement’s military wing. The Israeli military alleged that both men had participated in efforts to rebuild the movement’s military capabilities and had carried out plans to target Israeli civilians and forces both recently and during the war. The military accused Islamic Jihad of rebuilding military capabilities in violation of the ceasefire agreement and stated that Southern Command forces remain deployed in the area under the agreement to continue acting to remove any immediate threat.

parsed.headline: Algerian President says fighter jets were sent to Niger to thwart coup attempt

pages.text: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune stated that his country deployed fighter jets to Niamey in late August to help thwart a coup attempt. According to excerpts from an interview with local media outlets broadcast on Saturday, Tebboune said the warplanes were sent because certain parties had “gone too far,” though he did not specify if he was referring to internal or external actors. He described the situation as a “provocation against us.” The Algerian Ministry of Defence previously stated on August 30 that it had sent four fighter jets to Niger following unrest. Tebboune also noted that Niger’s Prime Minister, Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, had returned home from a visit to Algeria at night just before the mutiny occurred.

The reported coup attempt involved sustained gunfire and explosions in Niamey overnight from August 28 into August 29. Niger’s Minister of Defence, General Salifou Modi, announced that a group of military personnel attempted to detain colleagues at Air Base 101 and opened fire on strategic locations in the capital. The attacks targeted a military base at Diori Hamani International Airport, the state broadcaster, and the presidential palace. General Modi stated that security forces intervened and managed to contain the situation, gradually regaining control over the targeted locations.

parsed.headline: Somali President states country will not accept Israeli presence under any circumstances

pages.text: In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud stated that Somalia will not accept an Israeli presence in the country “under any circumstances” and will resist attempts to be pulled into Middle East crises. Mohamud described Israel as a “destabilising force” that does not abide by international law and stated, “We will overcome the challenges posed to our country by Israeli moves.”

Mohamud alleged that Israel is planning to establish a naval base in Berbera and utilize the city’s airport, suggesting the aim is to gain proximity to Iran and the Gulf states. Berbera is a port city on the Gulf of Aden coast in Somaliland, a self-declared republic in northwestern Somalia that Israel recognized last year, though the territory is claimed by Mogadishu. The president also criticized Tel Aviv’s recognition of Somaliland in December.

The president characterized Israeli plans as part of the “Greater Israel” project, a term for various proposals regarding Israeli control over territory beyond current borders. While Israel has not adopted this as official policy, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated in an August 2025 interview that he felt connected to the vision, an assertion that prompted condemnation from Arab governments. Berbera is located across the water from Yemen near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, an area where Iran-aligned Houthis have previously enforced a blockade on Israel-linked ships.

pages.text: Speaking at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, NPP flagbearer Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia stated that the cost of living in Ghana has risen massively despite a decline in the inflation rate. While acknowledging the recent easing in price pressures and the relative stability of the Ghanaian cedi, Dr. Bawumia observed that businesses still face significant difficulties and struggle with the costs of operating and sustaining their activities.

parsed.headline: Israeli journalists' verbal confrontation ends Republic of Ireland football news conference

pages.text: A news conference for Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson ended abruptly on Saturday following a confrontation with members of an Israeli media contingent. The incident occurred prior to a UEFA Nations League football match amid political tensions and protests regarding the fixture. Hallgrimsson later characterized the interaction as a “verbal attack.” During the event, an Israeli journalist asked Hallgrimsson for his views on a Flydubai aviation incident that occurred earlier in the week. The journalist asked, “What do you say about the people that you support? Their ideology is based on murder,” a question Al Jazeera reported as purportedly attempting to link Ireland’s stance on Palestine to the flight incident. Before the coach could respond, Football Association of Ireland communications manager Kieran Crowley intervened, requesting the journalist refrain from asking questions unrelated to the match. Crowley noted that while the association respected questions at a previous press conference, the current session was designated for football-related questions. The journalist persisted with the question before being stopped a second time by Crowley.

The aviation incident referenced during the press conference involved a Flydubai flight traveling from Dubai, UAE, to Tel Aviv, Israel, on September 30, 2026. According to the prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates, a co-pilot attempted to carry out a “terrorist act” by using an axe against the pilot to seize control of the aircraft. The plane, carrying 174 passengers, briefly plunged approximately 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before being brought back under control. The co-pilot wounded Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who had opened the cockpit door to seek assistance. While the attacker was not officially identified, media reports quoting unnamed sources identified him as an Omani national, Hamam al-Hammami.

parsed.headline: Dual UK-Iranian national released on bail following arrest in suspected RAF Fairford terror plot investigation

pages.text: A 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national has been released on bail following his arrest on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006. The individual was detained on October 1, 2026, in the London borough of Westminster, where searches of two properties have since concluded. He is the sixth person detained in connection with a suspected terrorist plot involving RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire. Five other British nationals, all in their mid-20s, were arrested last weekend and subsequently released on bail on September 28, 2026. Those initial arrests occurred after three suspicious vans were spotted near the military site, prompting a major security incident that included the evacuation of dozens of homes. Counter-terrorism police stated that while a quantity of petrol was found in the vans, no explosive devices were recovered. The investigation remains ongoing. Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, described the investigation as “hugely complex” and noted that specialist teams are interrogating multiple lines of inquiry, including the possibility of foreign state involvement. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated there were “strong indications” that Iran played a part in the incident near the Gloucestershire base, though he did not provide further details. Additionally, on October 1, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed that Israel had provided Britain with intelligence regarding the suspected terror plot.

parsed.headline: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia criticizes NDC government over unfulfilled promises

pages.text:
Addressing delegates at the NPP National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, former Vice President and NPP 2028 Presidential Candidate Dr Mahamudu Bawumia characterized nearly two years of the NDC administration as a series of failed and “scam” promises. Dr Bawumia stated that the government is struggling to fulfill many of its promises and has yet to provide convincing answers to questions raised by Ghanaians regarding its performance.

Dr Bawumia specifically cited the NDC's flagship 24-hour economy policy, noting that the promised job boom through the '1 job, 3 shifts, 3 people' (1-3-3) model has not materialized after nearly two years. He alleged that instead of job creation, the policy has resulted in the demolition of buildings for 24-hour markets. He also noted that the promised Women’s Development Bank has not opened to any market women in the nearly two years since the administration began.

Regarding economic costs, Dr Bawumia claimed that while the NDC promised reduced electricity tariffs under the 24-hour economy plan, there has instead been a dramatic increase in electricity tariffs. He further stated that despite inflation reportedly declining to 5% on paper, the cost of living for ordinary Ghanaians has increased due to rising costs for transportation, fuel, spare parts, and rent.

Dr Bawumia identified the relative stability of the cedi as the government's primary lifeline amidst these difficulties. He credited the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, which he recommended the Bank of Ghana launch in June 2021, as the major support behind the stability of the cedi and the subsequent easing of inflation and interest rates. He noted that key government officials had originally opposed the policy when it was introduced, claiming it was not feasible.
